messages:
sanjay: Quick experiment idea — blend capacity-optimized allocation with a conservative price cap in our mixed GPU pools to reduce interruptions without blowing cost targets.
laura: Can you sketch the actual bid curve/heuristic? numbers matter.
alex: Agree. Do you mean AWS capacity-optimized + maxPrice at X% of on-demand, or something else?
mei: Also need safe fallback logic: if capacity isn't available, fall back to cheaper region or on-demand pool with drain cooldown.
sanjay: Yeah, rough plan:
- primary: capacity-optimized allocationStrategy (prefer least-likely eviction)
- secondary: diversified instance types within same family
- price cap: maxPrice = 0.35 * on-demand
- fallback: after 30s of pending, route to reserved/ondemand pool with warm buffer
sanjay: Pseudocode for fleet chooser:
```
if capacityOptimized.available():
  request(allocationStrategy='capacity-optimized', maxPrice=0.35)
else:
  request(instanceTypes=diverse, maxPrice=0.25)
  if pending>30s:
    route_to(reserved_pool)
```
laura: How do we measure the trade-off? single metric: cost per successful token at SLO? interrupt rate? both.
alex: Let's capture: hourly cost, interruptions/hr, coldstart spillover, and downstream queue length.
mei: Also capture tail latency increase when spill to reserved. If warm buffer size is too small we just DDoS reserved.
ops-bot: simulation-run queued by @sanjay — ETA 20m. Args: {"region":"us-west-2","pool_mix":"75_spot/25_reserved","maxPriceFactor":0.35}
laura: sweet. if interruption drop is >10% for <5% cost increase, ship to prod flag.
alex: note — we should avoid hard-coded maxPrice for newer instance types; prefer relative pricing percentile (e.g., 30th percentile of last 24h) to avoid price spikes.
mei: Also add checkpoint frequency + small instance-level state writes to reduce wasted compute on eviction.
sanjay: Will post results. TL;DR: goal — 15-25% fewer interruptions with <8% cost delta.
ops-bot: sim complete: interruptions -18%, cost +4.2%, tail-latency +2.1% when spillover engaged. Full logs: https://internal.ops/sim/1955559999
laura: nice! let's run a second sim with maxPriceFactor=0.25 and 60s fallback to see sensitivity.
alex: can we run per-region analysis? eu-west seems tighter, might need different thresholds.
mei: I'll draft rollout plan: canary 1% traffic -> 5% -> 20% with automated rollback on interruption surge.
sanjay: thanks all — will open a runbook section for eviction handling + config defaults. :thumbsup:
